security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, DeFi protocol vocabulary, and /dev/null redirection. Real risks remain around package-manager plugin installation, outbound GitHub catalog probing, and downstream binary pre-flight installers that may place executables under hidden home-directory paths.

remediation.issue: Silent plugin installation expands the trust boundary to downstream plugins.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every new plugin install, including the plugin ID, source package, and reason for routing.

remediation.issue: Catalog probing uses shell commands and outbound GitHub API access during routing.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured plugin registry API provided by the host when available, and avoid shell pipelines for user-derived DApp names.

remediation.issue: Downstream plugins may request binary and script installation into hidden PATH locations.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the binary consent gate mandatory, show checksums when available, and never run curl, chmod, ln, or mkdir from plugin pre-flight text without approval.

remediation.issue: User-derived DApp names are used in regex-based catalog matching.
remediation.suggestion: Escape regex metacharacters or use exact structured comparisons after normalizing candidate plugin names.

content.user_title: Route DeFi DApp Requests to OKX Plugins
content.value_statement: Choosing the right DeFi plugin is hard when requests mention tokens, protocols, or Chinese aliases. This skill maps the request to a supported OKX plugin or asks a focused clarification.
actual_capabilities: Routes named requests for 20 supported DeFi DApps to their OKX plugin IDs.
Maps protocol-native tokens and phrases, such as HYPE, stETH, GHO, PT tokens, and CLANKER.
Uses Chinese aliases, trigger verbs, and routing examples from bundled reference files.
Separates install, clarification, discovery-table, and unknown-DApp catalog-probe flows.
Distinguishes pump.fun trade requests from pump.fun research requests.
Adds a consent gate before downstream plugins run binary pre-flight installers.
limitations: It does not replace the protocol knowledge inside each downstream OKX plugin.
Plugin installation and catalog probing may require network access and package-manager availability.
Some protocol variants are intentionally out of scope, such as Morpho Blue and GMX V1.
Generic DeFi requests may be clarified instead of routed automatically.

use_cases.title: Route A Named DeFi Action
use_cases.description: Send a protocol-specific action, such as staking on Lido or borrowing on Aave, to the matching OKX plugin.

use_cases.title: Compare Supported Protocols
use_cases.description: Handle requests that mention multiple DApps by asking whether to set up one plugin or discuss tradeoffs first.

use_cases.title: Support Chinese DApp Requests
use_cases.description: Resolve Chinese protocol aliases, action verbs, and examples to the correct routing outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Show Supported DApps
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me which DeFi DApps you can route and group them by category.

prompt_templates.title: Route A Named Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to deposit USDC into Aave V3. Route me to the right OKX plugin and continue with my request.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify A Generic Yield Request
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to earn yield with stablecoins. Ask one clarifying question if several supported DApps could fit.

prompt_templates.title: Probe An Unsupported DApp
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether there is an OKX plugin for <DApp name>. If not, show closest supported alternatives and the OKX DeFi fallback.

output_examples.output: The skill routes the request to the Lido plugin, loads it when available, and continues the staking request after consent checks.
The skill asks whether to set up Aave, set up Compound, or discuss the tradeoffs before installing anything.
The skill shows supported DApps grouped by category, including prediction markets, lending, perpetuals, swaps, staking, and meme launchpads.

best_practices: Name the target DApp when you want direct routing to a specific protocol plugin.
Include the action and token pair when a protocol-native token could mean several workflows.
Review binary install prompts before approving downstream plugin pre-flight steps.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic terms like swap or yield alone when you need a specific DApp.
Do not ask it for full protocol documentation that belongs in the downstream plugin.
Do not approve binary installs without checking the plugin name, release URL, and install path.

faq.question: Which DApps can this skill route?
faq.answer: It routes 20 listed DeFi DApps, including Polymarket, Aave, Hyperliquid, PancakeSwap, Curve, Lido, and pump.fun.

faq.question: Does it execute DeFi transactions by itself?
faq.answer: No. It routes the request to a downstream plugin, which owns its own commands, checks, and transaction flow.

faq.question: Can it handle Chinese requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Chinese aliases, action verbs, and routing examples for supported DApps and workflows.

faq.question: What happens when several DApps match?
faq.answer: It follows its routing rules, asks one clarification question, or shows supported options when no safe single route exists.

faq.question: What happens for an unsupported DApp?
faq.answer: It probes the plugin catalog for a matching plugin, then shows closest supported alternatives if no match exists.

faq.question: Why can installation require consent?
faq.answer: Some downstream plugins may download binaries or scripts. The skill tells agents to request explicit approval before running those installers.
